message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for SHORT_LINE.

Opponent p2 leads the SHORT_LINE auction at $54. I have $546 cash and am positioned at WATER_WORKS. The current bid increment is $55. I previously mortgaged Short Line for $100, so any purchase under $100 nets positive cash after mortgaging. I will bid up to $99.

If I drop now, p2 wins Short Line for $54 and mortgages it for $100. That nets them $46 cash. I will keep bidding to force them toward the $99 cap.

p2 is currently on SHORT_LINE. I will bid incrementally to $99 and drop at $100.

I considered jumping straight to $99 to end the auction quickly. But p2 has matched every bid from $1 to $54, so they will likely match all the way to $99 too. Incremental bidding is safer and still captures the same arbitrage.

I will bid $99. I started at $1, so I bid odd numbers; $99 is odd, meaning I would win at that price. The opponent would need $100 to beat me, and dropping there nets them only $1 profit. I own two mortgaged railroads, but Short Line does not add enough value to justify paying more than $100.

Unmortgaging my two railroads plus buying Short Line would cost too much. I need cash to survive p2's orange and dark blue monopolies. My light blue income engine is worth keeping.

I am at Water Works. Rolling a 2 lands on Park Place with three houses, charging $1100 rent. Rolling a 4 lands on Boardwalk with three houses, also charging $1100. Both are immediate threats.

Boardwalk with three houses costs $1400. I cannot afford that rent even if I liquidate all my properties. I am calculating the exact cash from selling my light blue houses and mortgaging those properties.

Selling all light blue houses yields $250. Mortgaging those properties plus States and Ventnor adds another $360. Total liquidation is $610. That still falls short of the $1100 rent on Park Place or Boardwalk.

I can barely afford Park Place even with full liquidation. Boardwalk is impossible to pay regardless. Winning Short Line for $99 nets only one dollar profit. That does not help me survive Boardwalk. The opponent already has $225 and their buildings are the real threat. I am dead if I roll a four.

Denying the opponent the railroad is not strategically critical. Even with Short Line, they would only have two railroads and pay $50 rent, which they cannot afford. The real value is extracting cash from them. Forcing them to pay $99 instead of $54 costs them $45.

I calculated the exact cash outcomes. If I win Short Line at $99, I end with $547. If I drop, they pay $54 and mortgage for $100, ending with $271. Continuing costs them $45 more than dropping. I am now checking whether keeping the railroad without mortgaging would leave them short on cash to survive my light blue rent.

Oriental with four houses pays $400. Vermont with three pays $270. Connecticut with three pays $300. I am now mapping the standard board positions from Short Line to see where p2 lands next.

From Short Line, p2 can roll a 10 to land on Oriental and pay $400 in rent. A roll of 12 lands on Vermont for $270. Their current cash of $225 is too low to cover either of those payments without liquidating.
